stem.en: On the Earth, an astronaut throws a ball straight up and it rises 8 m. The pull of gravity on the Moon is about one sixth of that on the Earth. How high does the same ball rise on the Moon, thrown up at the same speed?

text.en: About 1.3 m, because the weaker pull makes it rise less.
48 m, because the same energy lifts it six times higher.
8 m, because the speed and the mass are the same.
288 m, because six times is applied twice.

explanation.en: The ball starts with the same kinetic energy on both. At the top, all of it has become potential energy, mgh. The mass and the energy are the same, so g x h is the same. With g six times smaller, h is six times larger: 6 x 8 m = 48 m.

hints.en: At the top, kinetic energy = mgh. What stays the same on the Moon?
If g becomes six times smaller and mgh stays the same, what happens to h?
